collection.description: Two friends collapse laughing at the words the coconut, and a third villager asks what it means.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) only have to look at each other and say "the coconut," and they both collapse laughing. Nobody else knows why. Today, at lunch, it happens again, and (third), a third villager sitting with them, puts down (third.his/her) bowl and says, a little sadly, "What IS the coconut?"

text_only.reason: a small thing collapses in the story (a tower of shells, a pile); no building is damaged

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: (subject) tries. "So there was this coconut, and (friend) was standing under it, and... well, it didn't fall, that's the thing, it just..." (subject.He/She) stops. (friend) is crying with laughter. (third) is not laughing at all. "You had to be there," (subject) says weakly. That, everyone agrees, is the truest thing anyone has ever said about the coconut.

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: "We can't explain the coconut," says (friend). "But we can start a new one." Over the next hour, the three of them manage to make a small crab, a wet sandal and the word "absolutely" into something none of them can say without giggling. Nobody else in the village will ever understand it. That, it turns out, is the point.
